story: The state's no-cost 19,950-acre Houston land conveyance to AIDEA and the Senate Resources subpoena of DNR Commissioner John Crowther (lead), with University of Alaska AI principles and the Kenai Loop gas storage contest as backups

claims.claim: DNR proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres of state-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to AIDEA.
claims.verbatim: proposes to convey approximately 19,950 acres (subject parcel) of State-owned land in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA)
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment C Public Notice, page 29 of 47 (also the Executive Summary on page 1). Read from the showrunner's text extraction out/2026-10-16/sources/akleg_16978.txt. Corroborated by AIDEA's own fact sheet (docid 16980, 'Approximately 19,950 acres') and the Bullard memo. Sanity check: the three township aggregates in C13 to C15 sum to 19,934.83 acres, consistent with 'approximately 19,950'. The decision's cumulative impacts section says 'approximately 19,500 acres' once, which looks like a typo; do not use it. Background document, dated before the run window.

claims.claim: The Houston parcel lies approximately two miles north of the City of Houston.
claims.verbatim: approximately two miles north of the City of Houston in the Matanuska-Susitna Borough
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 2 of 47, Proposed Primary Action. AIDEA fact sheet (docid 16980) agrees ('About 2 miles north of Houston, Mat-Su Borough').

claims.claim: DNR would make the Houston conveyance noncompetitively and at no cost under AS 38.05.810(a), the Public and Charitable Use statute.
claims.verbatim: convey the subject parcel through a noncompetitive conveyance at no cost to AIDEA under Alaska Statute (AS) 38.05.810(a) Public and Charitable Use.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 2 of 47.

claims.claim: AIDEA would make no payment for the value of the Houston land but would cover administrative, survey, platting and closing costs.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA would make no payment for the value of the land, but remains responsible for administrative, survey, platting, and closing-related costs.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA) fact sheet, posted by the Senate Resources Committee
claims.notes: Location: page 1, 'What "no cost" means'. The fact sheet is dated 'July 2026' with no day printed, so 2026-07-01 is a month placeholder. DNR's decision footnote 1 agrees: AIDEA 'will not provide compensation for the value of the land' but pays administrative costs 'including but not limited to the costs of survey'.

claims.claim: DNR's preliminary decision says the commissioner shall waive the state's reversionary interest in the Houston land.
claims.verbatim: In this case, the commissioner shall waive the reversionary interest clause.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 17 of 47, Restrictions and Reservations item 3. This is a PRELIMINARY decision, so say 'proposes to waive' or 'would waive'. AIDEA's fact sheet says 'DNR proposes to waive the statutory reversionary interest'.

claims.claim: DNR wrote that keeping a reverter clause would limit AIDEA's ability to use its bonding authority and financing options.
claims.verbatim: would therefore limit the ability of AIDEA to fully exercise the bonding authority and financing options available under statute
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 21 of 47, Section XVI.C.

claims.claim: AS 38.05.810(g) requires the commissioner to retain a reversionary interest on these disposals unless it is waived by written determination.
claims.verbatim: shall retain a reversionary interest on each sale or other disposal granted under (a) or (e) of this section. The commissioner may waive the reversionary interest on a written determination
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, statute and regulation handout for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, subsection (g). Statute text as distributed by the committee. The waiver requires a finding 'that the waiver is in the public interest'.

claims.claim: DNR proposes to reclassify about 15,100 acres of the Houston parcel as Settlement land.
claims.verbatim: DNR proposes to reclassify 15,100 acres, more or less, within units P-01, P-02, P-03, H-06, U-01, and U-22a as Settlement.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 2 of 47, Land Classification Order. The committee's issues overview rounds this to 15,000 acres 'currently classified as forestry, habitat, and water resources'. Use DNR's 15,100.

claims.claim: DNR's preliminary decision states that its scope does not include AIDEA's use of the land after it is patented.
claims.verbatim: The scope of this decision does not include AIDEA’s post-patent use.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 5 of 47, Section IV. Quoted in the Bullard memo, footnote 18.

claims.claim: Scalable data centers are among the uses DNR's decision lists for AIDEA's proposed Houston district.
claims.verbatim: Development of scalable data centers that leverage existing and planned utility corridors.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 5 of 47 (also page 19, 'to develop scalable data centers'). This is a listed possible use and not a commitment. Pair it with C22 (AIDEA's 'possibilities, not commitments'), C28 (committee says AIDEA now says no data center is planned) and C52 (Ruaro called a data center 'implausible').

claims.claim: The parcel's northern boundary runs east along Deception Creek for about six miles to the foothills of the Talkeetna Mountains.
claims.verbatim: The northern boundary of the subject parcel runs east along Deception Creek for approximately six miles to the foot hills of the Talkeetna Mountains
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 6 of 47, Parcel Description. The boundary then turns south to bluffs above the Little Susitna River.

claims.claim: The parcel's western boundary lies approximately two miles east of the Parks Highway.
claims.value: two miles east of the Parks Highway
claims.verbatim: The western boundary of the subject parcel overlies section lines that are located approximately two miles east of the Parks highway.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 6 of 47.

claims.claim: The portion of the parcel in Township 18 North, Range 3 West totals about 7,375.87 acres.
claims.verbatim: Aggregating approximately 7,375.87 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment G Draft Land Classification Order, page 43 of 47, directly after the T18N R3W descriptions. Arithmetic check: 3,278.88 + 2,496.99 + 1,600 = 7,375.87.

claims.claim: The portion of the parcel in Township 19 North, Range 3 West totals about 4,172 acres.
claims.verbatim: Aggregating approximately 4,172 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment G, page 44 of 47. Made up of 4,096 acres of Tract A plus 76 acres of Lot 4 of U.S. Survey No. 4716, both 'located Southwesterly of Deception Creek'.

claims.claim: The portion of the parcel in Township 18 North, Range 2 West totals about 8,386.96 acres.
claims.verbatim: Aggregating approximately 8,386.96 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment G, page 44 of 47. Made up of 7,946.96 acres plus 440 acres. DNR's Survey Section calls this the 'Houston East Site' and lists it as UNSURVEYED.

claims.claim: About 1,600 acres of the parcel are described by a plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General's Office in Juneau in 1915.
claims.verbatim: according to the plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General’s Office in Juneau, Alaska, on December 4, 1915, containing approximately 1,600 acres, more or less.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment B Legal Description, page 27 of 47. Covers Sections 13 and 14 and part of Section 15 in T18N R3W. Only the T18N R3W pieces use the 1915 and 1917 Surveyor General plats. The rest of the parcel is described by BLM plats accepted in 1960, 1963, 1965 and 1966, so do not say the whole parcel was platted in 1915.

claims.claim: Other sections of the parcel are described by a plat approved by the U.S. Surveyor General's Office in Juneau in 1917.
claims.verbatim: ACCORDING TO THE PLAT APPROVED BY THE U.S. SURVEYOR GENERAL’S OFFICE IN JUNEAU, ALASKA, ON APRIL 2, 1917, CONTAINING APPROXIMATELY 3,278.88 ACRES, MORE OR LESS.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: Attachment B, page 27 of 47. Two T18N R3W tracts cite the April 2, 1917 plat, one of 3,278.88 acres and one of 2,496.99 acres.

claims.claim: DNR says the Little Susitna River south of the site flows at about 50 CFS in winter and up to 2,000 CFS in summer.
claims.verbatim: The Little Susitna River flows south of the project site and provides flows in the range of 50 CFS in the winter to 2,000 CFS in the summer months.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 9 of 47, Water Resources. Same section: residential wells in the area test at about five gallons per minute.

claims.claim: DNR counts approximately 41.8 miles of documented trails within the parcel that tie into networks such as the Haessler-Norris.
claims.verbatim: there are approximately 41.8 miles of documented trails within the subject parcel that tie into larger trail networks such as the Haessler-Norris.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: the sentence runs across the page 6 to 7 break, so a page header sits between 'documented' and 'trails' in the extraction. Same passage: 23.9 miles of forestry roads. This corroborates the committee's 'more than 40 miles' (C27).

claims.claim: DMLW Director Christy Colles signed the Houston preliminary decision for public notice on July 10th.
claims.verbatim: 7/10/2026 Approved by: Christy Colles Date of Signature Director Division of Mining, Land and Water
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 25 of 47. The original comment deadline was August 19th. The Bullard memo (footnote 26) and the SRES September 9th letter say it was extended to September 14th.

claims.claim: Sand, gravel and rock are not part of the state's mineral reservation and would go to AIDEA with the land.
claims.verbatim: The mineral estate reserved by the State does not include rock, gravel, or sand resources.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska DNR Division of Mining, Land and Water, Preliminary Decision ADL 234762
claims.notes: Location: page 15 of 47, Section XI. The same section says the disposal 'conveys to AIDEA the materials needed for surface development' and allows their use 'as an in-kind equity'. AIDEA's fact sheet agrees.

claims.claim: AIDEA's own fact sheet describes the listed uses for the Houston land as possibilities and not commitments.
claims.verbatim: These are possibilities, not commitments.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA) fact sheet, posted by the Senate Resources Committee
claims.notes: Location: page 2. The fact sheet is dated July 2026 with no day printed. It also says 'no specific end use has been definitively selected.'

claims.claim: The Senate Resources Committee's issues overview says 94 percent of other transfers under this statute were under 100 acres.
claims.verbatim: Ninety-four percent of other land transfers under this statute were under 100 acres, while this transfer covers about 31 square miles.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, 'What We Know at a Glance'. This is the committee majority's advocacy document and shows no underlying dataset. Attribute it, e.g. 'according to the committee's issues overview'.

claims.claim: The committee's issues overview says the Houston transfer covers about 31 square miles.
claims.verbatim: Of the 20,000 acres, or 31 square miles, 15,000 are currently classiﬁed as forestry, habitat, and water resources
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1. Arithmetic check: 19,950 acres divided by 640 is about 31.2 square miles. Alaska Public Media says 'approximately 30 square miles'. The 'ﬁ' ligature is as extracted.

claims.claim: The committee's issues overview says about 37 percent of the Houston area is wetlands.
claims.verbatim: About 37 percent of the area is wetlands.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, Local Impact. DNR's decision describes 'interspersed, non-contiguous wetlands' but gives no percentage. The 37 percent is the committee's figure only, so attribute it.

claims.claim: The committee's issues overview says the area holds more than 40 miles of public trails used for mushing, four-wheeling and snowmachining.
claims.verbatim: The area holds more than 40 miles of public trails for mushing, four-wheeling, and snowmachining.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1. Independently supported by DNR's 41.8 miles of documented trails (C19).

claims.claim: The committee's issues overview says AIDEA now says there is no data center planned.
claims.verbatim: AIDEA now says there is no data center planned.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, 'What is the Project'. This is the committee's characterization of AIDEA's position. It is consistent with Ruaro's reported testimony (C52, C53) and his July 30th letter (C45). Write it as 'the committee's overview says'.

claims.claim: The committee's issues overview says the Houston city council voted unanimously to oppose the land transfer.
claims.verbatim: The Houston city council voted unanimously to oppose the land transfer.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, Local Impact. Single source, and the committee is not the council, so I could not reach the council's own record. Attribute to the committee.

claims.claim: The Mat-Su Borough Assembly voted to oppose the Houston transfer.
claims.verbatim: Willow, Meadow Lakes, and the Mat-Su Borough Assembly have all voted in opposition.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media on October 15th, which cites the Mat-Su Sentinel: 'The Mat-Su Sentinel reports that the Mat-Su Borough Assembly voted last month to oppose the transfer.' The Mat-Su Sentinel's October 16th repost also carries this. The Willow and Meadow Lakes votes rest on the committee document alone.

claims.claim: According to the committee, the governor's SB 224 and HB 276, which sought below-market land transfers for commercial development, did not move from either Resources Committee.
claims.verbatim: The Governor introduced SB 224/HB276, which sought below-market land transfers for commercial development. Neither of those bill moved from either Resources Committee.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, Issues Overview for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1, Legal Concerns. I did not fetch the bill status pages because BASIS returns 403. Attribute to the committee.

claims.claim: DNR adopted its public purpose regulation, 11 AAC 98.010, on March 14th.
claims.verbatim: The regulation was adopted March 14, 2026 (Register 257).
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: memo page 3, footnote 9. Second primary source: the committee's statute handout (docid 16970) heads the regulation 'Adopted by DNR on 3/14/2026'. Giessel's office notes say DNR's notice of proposed changes was issued December 3, 2025, with a corrected supplemental notice on December 11, 2025.

claims.claim: Clause 4 of 11 AAC 98.010 counts support for private commerce or industry that contributes to economic development as a public purpose.
claims.verbatim: (4) supports private commerce or industry that contributes to the economic development of the state or any part of the state, including the creation, retention, or expansion of employment opportunities
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, statute and regulation handout for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 2. The same text is in the Bullard memo, footnote 8. Clause (5) adds 'is otherwise determined by the commissioner to be in the interest of the state.'

claims.claim: AS 38.05.810(a) requires the commissioner to ensure that disposals under it serve a public purpose and are in the public interest.
claims.verbatim: The commissioner shall ensure, by regulation, deed restriction, covenant, or otherwise, that disposals of land under this subsection serve a public purpose and are in the public interest.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee, statute and regulation handout for the October 8th hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 1. ADN's summary is 'allows no-cost land conveyances only for a public purpose'.

claims.claim: Senator Cathy Giessel sent Commissioner Crowther a public records request about the AIDEA and AHFC transfers on September 1st.
claims.verbatim: September 1, 2026 Dear Commissioner Crowther: Pursuant to the Alaska Public Records Act
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 5 of 6, the letter text. Page 2 of the timeline also lists 'September 1 – from Giessel to Crowther – public records request'. The document has no date of its own and was prepared for the October 14th hearing.

claims.claim: Giessel's office notes say DNR sent an initial response on September 10th and nothing after that.
claims.verbatim: September 10 – initial response from DNR to request for information
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 3 of 6. The next lines read 'No response thereafter.' This is Giessel's office's account, so attribute it. DNR's quoted reply says it would do the work 'as expeditiously as possible'.

claims.claim: On September 18th Giessel's office invited Crowther to the October 8th hearing, set for 1 to 3 p.m. at the Anchorage LIO.
claims.verbatim: September 18 Invite to Crowther Oct 8, from 1-3 PM, Anchorage LIO.
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 3 of 6. BASIS meeting pages could not be fetched (HTTP 403), so the 13:00 start time rests on this document.

claims.claim: On September 22nd Crowther's office declined the invitation, saying the governor's office had not given permission to attend.
claims.verbatim: We respectfully decline your invitation to participate in this upcoming Joint Resources Committee meeting. The Governor’s office has not given us permission to attend.
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 3 of 6. Corroborated by ADN on October 15th, which attributes the email to DNR legislative liaison Raymie Matiashowski ('The governor's office has not given us permission to attend'), and by KTUU. Alaska Public Media reports that the governor's office would not say why.

claims.claim: On October 9th Giessel invited Crowther to speak to Senate Resources on October 26th at 10 a.m. at the Anchorage LIO.
claims.verbatim: I am extending an invitation to you to speak to the Senate Resources Committee on October 26, 10 AM, at the Anchorage LIO.
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 3 of 6. On October 10th Crowther replied 'received and we will be back in touch with you soon', and the notes add 'No response thereafter.'

claims.claim: On October 13th Giessel's office repeated its September 1st request for information to DNR.
claims.verbatim: October 13 to DNR: repeat request for information requested on Sept 1.
claims.source_outlet: Office of Senator Cathy Giessel, Discussion Notes and Timeline for the October 14th SRES hearing
claims.notes: Location: page 4 of 6.

claims.claim: A September 4th Legislative Legal Services memo says DNR limited its review to exclude AIDEA's use of the land after conveyance.
claims.verbatim: DNR has limited the scope of its review to exclude AIDEA's use after conveyance.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: page 1, Short Answer. Work Order No. 35-LS0103, from Legislative Counsel Alpheus Bullard to Sen. Giessel. Background document, dated before the run window. The scout quoted this with an ellipsis, so use the full sentences in C40 and C41.

claims.claim: The Bullard memo concludes that without an analysis of likely uses the conveyance may raise legal issues.
claims.verbatim: Because determining whether the conveyance serves a public purpose may require an evaluation of the likely uses to which the land will be put, without this analysis, the conveyance may raise legal issues.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: page 1. The memo is hedged ('may'), so keep the hedge. The same memo also says 'DNR has the authority to convey land to AIDEA if the conveyance is for a public purpose.' Cover both for balance. ADN's Alaska Journal of Commerce also quotes 'may raise legal issues'.

claims.claim: The Bullard memo says the statute sets no limit on the amount of land that may be conveyed.
claims.verbatim: There is no limitation on the amount of land that may be conveyed under this authority.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: page 2.

claims.claim: Bullard wrote that he was not aware of any prior transfer of land to AIDEA under AS 38.05.810.
claims.verbatim: I am not aware of any prior transfer of land to AIDEA under AS 38.05.810.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: page 2. This is Bullard's stated awareness and not an established fact, so keep the framing 'he was not aware'.

claims.claim: Bullard wrote that without a reversionary interest there is no post-patent legal mechanism to keep the land serving a public purpose.
claims.verbatim: If DNR does not maintain a revisionary interest in the land, there is no post-patent legal mechanism to ensure that the land continues to serve a public purpose.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Legislative Legal Services memo by Alpheus Bullard
claims.notes: Location: page 6, footnote 21. 'revisionary' is the memo's own spelling.

claims.claim: In a July 30th letter quoted by the committee, AIDEA Executive Director Randy Ruaro wrote that no project had been approved or selected.
claims.verbatim: No project has been approved or selected. There is no committed data-center tenant, industrial developer, site plan power source, cooling system, water-supply plan, or construction schedule.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Senate Resources Committee letter to Commissioner Crowther
claims.notes: Location: page 2. This is Ruaro's July 30th letter to Rep. Kevin McCabe as quoted in the committee's September 9th letter. The original letter is on Facebook and was not fetched, so say 'as quoted by the committee'. 'site plan power source' is the letter's text as printed.

claims.claim: The Senate Resources Committee voted on Wednesday, October 14th, to subpoena Commissioner Crowther.
claims.verbatim: legislators on the Senate Resources Committee voted Wednesday to issue a subpoena
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Eric Stone. Published Thursday October 15th, so 'Wednesday' is October 14th. Independently corroborated by ADN (Iris Samuels, October 15th) and Alaska's News Source/KTUU (Hannah Lee, October 14th). BASIS lists an SRES meeting at 10:00 on October 14th, but that page returned 403 to me. No primary record of the vote was reachable.

claims.claim: Five senators voted in favor of the subpoena during the October 14th meeting.
claims.verbatim: The subpoena passed with five yays.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Vote count resolution. ADN says the committee 'voted 5-0', that Sen. George Rauscher 'abstained from voting', and that Sen. Robb Myers 'did not attend the meeting'. KTUU says 'five yays', that Rauscher, attending virtually, did not vote, and that he was later allowed to email a 'yes' for the record. Both agree on five yes votes cast in the meeting. They disagree on Rauscher (abstained, or lost connection and later emailed yes). Do NOT say 'unanimous' or '6-0'. The safest deck phrasing is 'voted to subpoena', or 'five senators voted yes, according to ADN and KTUU'. KTUU's page shows 'Updated Oct. 14, 2026 at 4:36 PM AKDT', while its URL carries the UTC date.

claims.claim: Sen. Bill Wielechowski made the motion to subpoena Crowther.
claims.verbatim: Sen. Bill Wielechowski moved to issue a subpoena requiring Crowther to attend the next meeting
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Single source. KTUU adds that the subpoena also covers the requested public records. Use 'according to KTUU'.

claims.claim: DNR confirmed on Thursday, October 15th, that Crowther would appear at the October 26th hearing.
claims.verbatim: The department confirmed Thursday that Commissioner John Crowther would appear at a hearing on Oct. 26
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Corroborated by ADN: 'Henry and Giessel confirmed on Thursday that Crowther had agreed to appear before the committee later this month' (Lorraine Henry is DNR's spokesperson). No DNR statement was reachable directly.

claims.claim: The committee's next meeting is scheduled for October 26th at 10 a.m.
claims.verbatim: The next meeting is scheduled for Oct. 26 at 10 a.m.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Corroborated by the primary Giessel invitation in C38 ('October 26, 10 AM, at the Anchorage LIO'). The scout's 'Denali Room' detail could not be verified because BASIS returned 403, so it is killed.

claims.claim: AIDEA Executive Director Randy Ruaro testified on October 8th that the rumored data center is implausible because there is no excess energy supply.
claims.verbatim: the rumored data center is “implausible” because there is no excess energy supply
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: As reported, since no hearing transcript or recording was reached. Alaska Public Media independently reports that 'AIDEA's executive director' said 'hosting a data center on the site was "implausible."' The only verbatim word is 'implausible'. The rest is KTUU's paraphrase, so do not put it in quotation marks as Ruaro's words.

claims.claim: KTUU reports that Ruaro testified that no developer, tenant, power source or site plan exists for the Houston land.
claims.value: no developer, tenant, power source or site plan
claims.verbatim: testified that no developer, tenant, power source, or site plan exists for the land
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: KTUU paraphrase. It matches Ruaro's own July 30th letter (C45), which says there is no committed tenant, developer, site plan or power source.

claims.claim: Giessel said the transfer is a violation of the Legislature's appropriation authority.
claims.verbatim: This is a violation of our legislative appropriation authority,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media
claims.notes: Verbatim quote of a named person as printed by Alaska Public Media. KTUU prints a longer version: 'So actually this is a violation of our legislative appropriation authority'. This is Giessel's legal opinion and not a finding, so present it as her quote.

claims.claim: Giessel said one of her big concerns is that this is a huge conveyance of public land.
claims.verbatim: One of my big concerns is this is a huge conveyance of public land.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News
claims.notes: Iris Samuels. The page prints 'Published October 15, 2026' although the URL path is dated 10/14. The follow-on sentence 'That land has value.' appeared in my first fetch but could not be confirmed character for character on re-fetch, so quote only the first sentence.

claims.claim: Giessel said the University of Alaska charges a private Mat-Su developer $586,740 a year to lease 829 acres.
claims.verbatim: She said the University of Alaska charges a private Mat-Su developer $586,740 a year to lease 829 acres.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: This verifies that Giessel SAID it, not that UA collects it now. The Mat-Su Sentinel (October 6th) reports that Terra Energy's 20-year UA lease pays $20,000 in year one and $60,000 in years two and three, rising to $586,000 per year only once operations begin, which is targeted for 2030 (C57). Must be phrased as Giessel's comparison, e.g. 'Giessel pointed to a UA lease she said will pay about $586,740 a year once operating'.

claims.claim: Giessel estimated the nearly 20,000 acres are worth roughly $14 million a year in foregone state revenue.
claims.verbatim: the land is worth roughly $14 million a year, which she claims would be foregone state general fund revenue.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source (KTUU)
claims.notes: Her estimate, not an appraisal. Arithmetic check: $586,740 divided by 829 acres is about $708 per acre per year, and times 19,950 acres that is about $14.1 million, so it extrapolates the UA lease rate in C55. That rate is a future post-operations rent. Alaska Public Media and ADN say only 'millions'. Phrase as 'Giessel estimated'.

claims.claim: Terra Energy's payment on its 829-acre UA lease near Port MacKenzie would increase to $586,000 a year once operations begin.
claims.verbatim: the payment would increase to $586,000 per year
claims.source_outlet: Mat-Su Sentinel
claims.notes: Tim Bradner and Amy Bushatz. Same article: 'Terra Energy has leased 829 acres of University of Alaska land', a 20-year lease signed in late May, $20,000 in the first year and $60,000 in years two and three, operations targeted for 2030, with a 2 percent annual inflation adjustment. killed.claim: The subpoena vote was unanimous, or 6-0 with Rauscher.

killed.claim: The University of Alaska charges $586,740 a year for 829 acres, stated as a present fact.
killed.why: It is only Giessel's statement as reported by KTUU. The Mat-Su Sentinel reports that the lease pays $20,000 in year one and reaches $586,000 a year only once operations begin, targeted for 2030. It survives only as an attributed claim (C55) with context (C57).

killed.claim: The University of Alaska lease covers 829.34 acres.

Superseded by the primary DNR figure of 15,100 acres (C08). The committee's figure is a rounding.
